lead: A QR code, drawn as SVG (also rendered on the server, sharp at any scale). The encoder is our own, with no dependencies: numeric / alphanumeric / UTF-8 modes, versions 1–40 and all four error correction levels.

status.title: Status
status.note: Click Refresh to simulate fetching a new code: after an 800 ms spinner the content changes (token=`{n}`).

wechat.title: WeChat login flow
wechat.description: For a WeChat login, the QR code holds a WeChat link your backend gets, and its status comes from polling the backend; the component's loading / active / scanned / expired map onto that flow. A timer and buttons stand in for it here.
wechat.done: **Logged in.** Once confirmed on the phone, the backend hands the session to the frontend (usually a token, after polling sees "confirmed").

hint.active: Scan with WeChat to log in (expires in {left}s)
hint.scanned: Scanned — confirm the login on your phone

wechat.wait: Do nothing and the countdown runs out: the QR code expires, and Refresh fetches a new one.

styling.title: Styling Reference
styling.description: A theme style's `qrcode.css` styles the frame (border, padding, radius, shadow) and the status mask; the code's own dark / background colors are functional colors for scanning and don't follow the theme.
styling.root: The frame; carries `data-bordered` / `data-status`, and `data-error` when the content doesn't fit; the padding ring's background reads `--qr-bg`
styling.svg: The SVG, the background rect and every dark module (one path); their colors are `fill` attributes, not set by the theme style
styling.icon: The icon in the middle and its backing
styling.mask: The status mask (`data-status`), the spinner and the notice text; the refresh button is a Button
